summary: Discovery / POC scoping call with Quantum Payments to decide between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private for a payments fraud-detection assistant. Main concerns: latency (<=150ms tail), cost per 1M tokens/month, data residency and KMS, and pilot scope (100 req/s steady, 300 burst). Agreed to run benchmarks and exchange network/security docs; Redwood to send pricing and Dedicated sizing. Decision timeline ~6 weeks contingent on benchmark results.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-26
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Head of Platform, Quantum Payments), Diego Marquez (ML Eng), Priya Patel (Security Lead)
---
Summary (auto): Discussed POC pilot scope and decision criteria between Hosted / Dedicated / Private; agreed on benchmarks and next steps.
---
[00:00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, can we do quick intros? I'm Lena, AE on the account, with Marcus who will do the technical deep dive.
[00:00:12] Aisha Khan: Hi, Aisha here, Head of Platform at Quantum Payments. Diego and Priya are on as well.
[00:00:18] Diego Marquez: Diego, ML eng, I'll own the benchmark work with you.
[00:00:21] Priya Patel: Priya, security lead, will be the contact for compliance questions.
[00:00:26] Marcus Chen: Marcus, Redwood SE, nice to meet you — we'll focus on sizing and runbook.
[00:00:33] Lena Park: High level, Quantum wants to embed an assistant into your merchant portal for fraud triage and alerts. We got some notes from Aisha on traffic but want to confirm success criteria and whether Hosted / Dedicated / Private makes sense.
[00:00:46] Aisha Khan: Correct, ideally the assistant will be inline for ops — we need low tail latency, 95-99 PCTL under 200ms ideally, and strict data residency for EU transactions. Also cost matters, we have a target: keep infra + inference under $X per 1M tokens but that's flexible.
[00:01:05] Marcus Chen: Ok, good. Quick clarifying Qs: what's your request profile today? QPS, payload sizes, typical context window?
[00:01:12] Aisha Khan: We're targeting 100 steady req/s during peak, with 200-300 bursts for 5-10 minutes. Average input size ~250 tokens, responses ~120 tokens. We may increase to 150 steady after pilot.
[00:01:27] Lena Park: Great, that's helpful. For pilot we usually recommend 2-4 weeks bench + 4-week evaluation. Decision timeline?
[00:01:35] Aisha Khan: Want a decision within ~6 weeks. Pilot should start within two weeks if the bench goes well.
[00:01:42] Diego Marquez: On the performance side, we need tail latency under 200ms for 95th and graceful degradation after that. Also consistency across EU region.
[00:01:51] Marcus Chen: Ok, so options: Hosted (fastest time to value) — Redwood Hosted API with regional routing; Dedicated — reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolation; Private — VPC or on-prem where control plane is customer-managed. Each has tradeoffs for latency, cost, and compliance.
[00:02:07] Priya Patel: For security, we need SOC 2, SSO/SAML integration, and KMS/HSM for key control. Also audit logs and retention controls.
[00:02:16] Marcus Chen: Redwood supports SOC2, SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs. For KMS we have integrations and bring-your-own-key options; in Private you can have more direct HSM/KMS control.
[00:02:27] Aisha Khan: So securitywise Private would be ideal but it's heavier ops. We're open to Dedicated if it meets data residency and KMS constraints.
[00:02:35] Lena Park: Right. Let's walk through workload sizing and a benchmark plan. Marcus?
[00:02:40] Marcus Chen: Based on 100 req/s steady, 250 input + 120 output tokens, that's roughly 100*(370 tokens) = 37k tokens/sec ~ 2.22M tokens/minute, wait that's off - sorry, math slip. Let's do per second: 370 tokens per request * 100 req/s = 37k tokens/s, that's a lot — oh, I'm mixing tokens/min and tokens/sec. If we assume 100 req/s * 370 tokens = 37,000 tokens/s which is 2.22M tokens/min — that's high. Are you sure about tokens?
[00:03:15] Diego Marquez: Yeah that sounds high because of our input encoding; many of our payloads are structured JSON but shorter after summarization. Maybe realistic average is 80 tokens input + 120 output => 200 tokens/request.
[00:03:28] Marcus Chen: Ok, 200 tokens * 100 req/s = 20k tokens/s which is 1.2M tokens/min — still in the scale but manageable for Dedicated pools. For Hosted, cost will scale linearly; for Dedicated we size GPUs for throughput target and use batching + KV cache to reduce repeated prefix cost.
[00:03:44] Lena Park: Important decision criteria we heard: latency SLO (95/99 PCTL), predictable cost, data residency/KMS, and time-to-market. Does that capture it?
[00:03:52] Aisha Khan: Yes, plus supportability and runbooks for incidents.
[00:03:55] Priya Patel: Also auditability and the ability to erase PII on request.
[00:03:58] Marcus Chen: For PII we can set retention policies, and in Dedicated we can isolate logs to customer storage; in Private you manage retention fully.
[00:04:08] Diego Marquez: Benchmarks: we want an end-to-end test (our app -> Redwood -> app) using our test traffic profile. Measure latencies (p50/p95/p99), throughput sustained for 30m, and cost per 1M tokens.
[00:04:20] Marcus Chen: Agreed. We'll propose a bench that runs Hosted first for baseline, then Dedicated sizing run to show improvements in latency/cost. For Private we can do architecture review and simulated run unless you can host early.
[00:04:33] Aisha Khan: We cannot host on-prem for pilot window, so Private is out for immediate pilot but remains possible later.
[00:04:39] Lena Park: Timeline proposal: Redwood sends pricing + bench plan 3 business days; you send traffic profile and sample test dataset; we run baseline Hosted bench within a week; Dedicated bench next week after sizing; review results and meet to decide. Does that work?
[00:04:52] Aisha Khan: Sounds good.
[00:04:54] Priya Patel: Quick Q on encryption: do you support envelope encryption with our KMS?
[00:04:59] Marcus Chen: Yes — both Hosted and Dedicated support BYOK integrations (KMS), with a caveat: Hosted uses brokered envelope keys unless you opt for Dedicated or Private which can connect to customer KMS for direct key control. We'll send the KMS integration doc.
[00:05:13] Priya Patel: And network? VPC peering or private link?
[00:05:16] Marcus Chen: We support PrivateLink and VPC peering for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can use region restrictions and IP allowlists but is less ideal for strict VPC-only workflows.
[00:05:26] Diego Marquez: On model selection — are you providing model catalog and quantized variants? Our concern is cost vs quality.
[00:05:33] Marcus Chen: Redwood provides curated open models and we can run the same eval sets across model variants. For Dedicated we can pin to quantized runtimes (4-bit/8-bit) to lower cost while measuring quality regressions. We'll include recommendations in the bench report.
[00:05:46] Aisha Khan: Another question: how does autoscaling work for Dedicated?
[00:05:50] Marcus Chen: Dedicated pools can autoscale within reserved boundaries and burst to shared capacity; policy is configurable. For strict throughput you can set min capacity/guaranteed GPUs.
[00:05:59] Lena Park: Diego, what's the minimum SLA you'd require to move from Hosted to Dedicated?
[00:06:03] Diego Marquez: We need 99.9% availability for the inference path during business hours and consistent p99 latencies below 350ms. Ideally p99 < 250ms.
[00:06:12] Marcus Chen: That aligns with Dedicated SLAs; Hosted may have region-level variability but generally meets business use cases. We'll include historic p95/p99 numbers in the doc.
[00:06:21] Aisha Khan: On cost transparency — can you give a breakdown token-level and per-route?
[00:06:27] Lena Park: Yes Redwood Console provides token-level cost and route breakdowns; in Dedicated you'll get clearer unit economics since you're paying for capacity.
[00:06:36] Priya Patel: Anything on data residency for logs and KV cache?
[00:06:40] Marcus Chen: For Dedicated we can ensure logs and caches stay in the EU region and route to your storage. Hosted will store logs per region but in some cases metadata may be routed to control plane in other regions — we'll confirm in the security doc.
[00:06:54] Aisha Khan: Ok, on success criteria for the pilot we propose: 1) p95 < 150ms, p99 < 300ms for EU transactions; 2) sustained 100 req/s with <=10% error rate; 3) cost target within X% of our budget; 4) SOC2 & KMS integration validated.
[00:07:14] Marcus Chen: That’s good — we'll validate feasibility. Some of those latencies depend on model choice and quantization tradeoffs. We'll run both quality and latency evals.
[00:07:24] Diego Marquez: For evaluation metrics, include ROC/AUC on fraud detection, false positive rate, and human-in-the-loop latency.
[00:07:31] Lena Park: Noted. Let's talk benchmarks in more detail — proposed tests: synthetic load to target QPS, realistic payloads from Diego, cold-start and steady-state, and KV cache hit-rate simulation.
[00:07:43] Marcus Chen: We'll instrument with request IDs and tracing so you can see per-token breakdowns. Also include continuous batching and prefix caching to show cost reductions.
[00:07:52] Aisha Khan: For the Dedicated sizing, what's the rough GPU count for our profile?
[00:07:56] Marcus Chen: Rough estimate: if we're at 100 req/s with 200 tokens/request and a medium model, we might need a small pool of 2-4 A100-equivalent GPUs with batching; exact size will come from the bench. We'll give a range.
[00:08:09] Diego Marquez: Any limitations on model versions or KV cache retention?
[00:08:12] Marcus Chen: KV cache retention configurable; model versions can be pinned and rollouts supported. We'll document rollback policies too.
[00:08:20] Priya Patel: We will need an NDA addendum for some of the app-specific telemetry in logs.
[00:08:25] Lena Park: We can send a template.
[00:08:28] [00:08:28] <cross talk>
[00:08:29] Aisha Khan: Quick operational Q — does Redwood provide runbooks for incidents and who we contact?
[00:08:33] Marcus Chen: Yes, Redwood provides runbooks and an on-call support path for Dedicated customers; Hosted has standard support tiers. We'll include RACI and escalation steps in the packet.
[00:08:43] Diego Marquez: For the bench dataset we will send a 10k sample set covering common and edge cases.
[00:08:48] Lena Park: Great. I'll recap next steps at the end.
[00:08:52] [00:08:52] --- mid-call technical dive ---
[00:09:00] Marcus Chen: Diving into bench details: we'll run three model variants — baseline open model A, quantized variant of A, and a bigger model B for quality comparison. For each collect p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and unit cost.
[00:09:18] Diego Marquez: Can you simulate burst behavior? We need to understand tail latency under burst.
[00:09:22] Marcus Chen: Yes, we'll include a burst profile test and show how autoscaling behaves; also show fallbacks to smaller model variants to maintain latency at cost trade-offs.
[00:09:31] Aisha Khan: How long do you need to run each bench?
[00:09:35] Marcus Chen: For steady-state, we prefer 30 minutes per run; for burst tests, repeated 10-minute bursts. End-to-end including analysis expect 5 business days.
[00:09:44] Lena Park: Ok we have about 30 minutes left, any remaining security concerns?
[00:09:49] Priya Patel: Ensure we can redact certain fields in logs and that audit logs include full request IDs. Also CCPA/DSR concerns for EU customers.
[00:09:58] Marcus Chen: We support redaction and will show how logs are partitioned. For DSR we have documented processes.
[00:10:05] Aisha Khan: If benchmark shows Dedicated improves p99 by 30% and cost reduces by 20% we will likely choose Dedicated. If not, we may start with Hosted and plan Dedicated for phase 2.
[00:10:15] Lena Park: Good rule of thumb. We'll target that improvement.
[00:10:19] [00:10:19] --- final recap ---
[00:10:20] Lena Park: Recap: Redwood to send pricing + Dedicated sizing estimates, Marcus to send bench plan and model/eval details, Quantum to send traffic profile and 10k test samples, Priya to confirm KMS and SSO provider. Benchmark run targeted next Wed (2026-04-01). Decision timeline ~6 weeks.
[00:10:41] Aisha Khan: Confirmed.
[00:10:43] Priya Patel: Confirmed.
[00:10:45] Marcus Chen: We'll also include a short doc comparing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for your exact profile.
[00:10:50] Lena Park: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.
[00:10:54] Diego Marquez: Thanks, talk soon.
[00:10:56] [END]
